steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Natural fibres: cotton (breathable, absorbent, soft), wool (warm, elastic, fire-resistant), silk (strong, lustrous, drapes well), linen (cool, crisp, creases easily). | Key Fact: Synthetic fibres: polyester (durable, quick-dry, wrinkle-resistant), nylon (strong, abrasion-resistant), elastane/Lycra (extreme stretch and recovery). | Key Fact: Woven fabrics: warp and weft interlaced at 90 degrees - stable, strong, limited stretch. Plain weave, twill weave (denim), satin weave. | Key Fact: Knitted fabrics: interlocking loops - stretchy, comfortable, can ladder. Weft knit (t-shirts) vs warp knit (more stable, swimwear).

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why polycotton is used for school shirts instead of 100% cotton or 100% polyester. | Compare woven and knitted fabric constructions, explaining why each suits different garments. | Discuss the environmental impact of synthetic fibres compared to natural fibres.
